text: Company, villainous company, hath been the spoil of me.
plain: The people you run with are what ruin you.

text: Honour is a mere scutcheon. And so ends my catechism.
plain: Reputation is a painted shield. The dead don't feel it and the living won't keep it.

text:
O gentlemen, the time of life is short!
To spend that shortness basely were too long
If life did ride upon a dial’s point,
Still ending at the arrival of an hour.
plain: Life is short, so spending it small and cheap is a waste even if you only had an hour.
Losing to a rival hurts the pride more than any wound hurts the body.

text:
But thoughts, the slaves of life, and life, time’s fool,
And time, that takes survey of all the world,
Must have a stop.
plain: Your thoughts serve your life, your life serves time, and time ends for everything.

text:
Ill-weaved ambition, how much art thou shrunk!
When that this body did contain a spirit,
A kingdom for it was too small a bound;
But now two paces of the vilest earth
Is room enough.
plain: The man who thought a kingdom was too small now needs two paces of dirt.

text:
Two stars keep not their motion in one sphere,
Nor can one England brook a double reign,
Of Harry Percy and the Prince of Wales.
plain: Two people can't both be number one in the same place.

text: The better part of valour is discretion, in the which better part I have saved my life.
plain: Knowing when to back off is half of courage. Falstaff just uses it as an excuse.

text: I can get no remedy against this consumption of the purse. Borrowing only lingers and lingers it out, but the disease is incurable.
plain: Borrowing doesn't cure being broke. It only drags the sickness out.

text: A good wit will make use of anything. I will turn diseases to commodity.
plain: A sharp mind finds a way to use even its own bad luck.

text: Care I for the limb, the thews, the stature, bulk, and big assemblance of a man? Give me the spirit, Master Shallow.
plain: Size and muscle mean little. Pick the person with spirit.

text:
When we mean to build,
We first survey the plot, then draw the model,
And when we see the figure of the house,
Then we must rate the cost of the erection,
Which if we find outweighs ability,
What do we then but draw anew the model
In fewer offices, or at least desist
To build at all?
plain: Count the cost before you build, and shrink the plan if you can't afford it.

text:
An habitation giddy and unsure
Hath he that buildeth on the vulgar heart.
plain: Build on the crowd's love and you're building on sand.

text:
O thoughts of men accursed!
Past and to come seems best; things present, worst.
plain: People always praise the past and the future and complain about right now.

text: We are time’s subjects, and time bids be gone.
plain: Time is the boss and it says move.

text:
Yet the first bringer of unwelcome news
Hath but a losing office, and his tongue
Sounds ever after as a sullen bell,
Remember’d tolling a departing friend.
plain: Whoever brings bad news gets hated for it, like a bell that tolls a death.
You knew the odds were bad when you went in. Capsized, you go out again.

text: Well, thus we play the fools with the time, and the spirits of the wise sit in the clouds and mock us.
plain: We waste our days acting the fool while wiser people look down and laugh.

text: Let the end try the man.
plain: Judge me by how it all ends, not by how it looks now.

text: Is it not strange that desire should so many years outlive performance?
plain: The wanting outlasts the ability to do anything about it.

text: Peace, good Doll, do not speak like a death’s-head; do not bid me remember mine end.
plain: Nobody wants the reminder that they're going to die, which is why they need it.

text:
By heaven, Poins, I feel me much to blame,
So idly to profane the precious time,
When tempest of commotion, like the south
Borne with black vapour, doth begin to melt
And drop upon our bare unarmed heads.
plain: The storm is about to break and you're out here wasting precious time.

text:
There is a history in all men’s lives
Figuring the natures of the times deceased;
The which observed, a man may prophesy,
With a near aim, of the main chance of things
As yet not come to life, who in their seeds
And weak beginning lie intreasured.
plain: Study the past and you can predict what's coming, because everything starts as a small seed.

text:
Are these things then necessities?
Then let us meet them like necessities;
plain: If it can't be avoided, face it like something that can't be avoided.

text: Certain, ’tis certain, very sure, very sure. Death, as the Psalmist saith, is certain to all, all shall die.
plain: Death is certain for everyone, so what are you saving yourself for?

text: A man can die but once. We owe God a death.
plain: You only die once and it's already owed, so don't live like a coward.

text: We have heard the chimes at midnight, Master Shallow.
plain: We have had our wild nights and they are gone.
A real peace is a win for both sides because nobody has to lose.

text:
Will Fortune never come with both hands full,
But write her fair words still in foulest letters?
She either gives a stomach and no food—
Such are the poor, in health; or else a feast
And takes away the stomach—such are the rich,
That have abundance and enjoy it not.
plain: Luck gives you the appetite or the meal, never both. The poor are hungry, the rich can't enjoy it.

text: Thou seek’st the greatness that will overwhelm thee.
plain: The big thing you chase may be the thing that crushes you.

text: Thy wish was father, Harry, to that thought.
plain: You believed it because you wanted it to be true.
